summary: Clean, small implementation. All 39 authored strings (7 postflop templates, 6 contexts, 7 preflop sentences, 9 seat names, 10 definitions) match spec §5 exactly; checked by a script against spec.md. explainPreflop and explainPostflop follow the §5 rules, including call-capped, the alternative-then-borderline order and the pot-odds-fold-implied key. The tests are not tautological. Unit tests pin exact copy using hard-coded definition strings, not values read back from CONCEPTS. The acceptance oracle checks that the first sentence naming each concept contains its definition, so it would fail if a definition moved or a template named a concept without defining it. The sentence split /(?<=[.!?])\s+/ only splits on punctuation followed by whitespace, so 20.5%, UTG+1 and '(just called the big blind)' never split a sentence wrongly. A scan of 30,000 extra decisions (seed 9999) found every rule and situation variant reading correctly, no check-free text with calling-range equity above 50%, and no value-bet with a non-zero required equity. Determinism is covered by AC#5. Bot cost is negligible: the 10k-hand playtest took 14.48/14.53 s on the branch vs 14.37/14.44 s on base c45d053 (about +0.1 s, under the 15 s budget), and the SHA is unchanged (14d746f7...2e48) with 0 invariant violations. The locked re-pins add one entry each with no assertion removed; the TASK-7.2 sandbox gains the 8 files that explain.ts's type imports pull in. One open risk: the acceptance file takes about 7.7-8.2 s locally, right at the D-6 threshold (MINOR, optional split). No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
